title: 2026 U.S. House election in Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District
description: The 2026 general election for Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District pits seven-term Republican incumbent French Hill against Democratic nominee Chris Jones. The district covers central Arkansas including most of Little Rock and all of Cleburne, Conway, Faulkner, Perry, Saline, Van Buren, and White counties. Hill chairs the powerful House Financial Services Committee, while Jones is a nuclear engineer and former Democratic gubernatorial nominee. The race is rated Solid/Safe Republican by major nonpartisan forecasters, though a May 2026 poll showed Jones leading Hill by 3 points among likely voters. In June 2026, former U.S. Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg endorsed Jones and campaigned with him at a Little Rock rally on Juneteenth.
polling_note: Only one poll was found for this race as of late May 2026, commissioned by the Jones campaign and conducted by 2040 Strategy Group. No independent public polls were available.

candidates.name: French Hill
candidates.summary: French Hill is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2014. He chairs the House Financial Services Committee and previously served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Treasury and Executive Secretary to President George H.W. Bush's Economic Policy Council. A ninth-generation Arkansan and former community banker, Hill is running on a platform of tax cuts, border security, and conservative economic policy.

Healthcare.stance: French Hill supports targeted, transparent health-care reforms to lower costs by encouraging innovation, increasing competition and choice, reforming medical malpractice laws, and reducing waste, fraud, and abuse. He also advocates empowering individuals with health savings accounts and ensuring affordable coverage for people with pre-existing conditions, while expanding community and teaching health centers to improve access, especially in rural Arkansas.

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: French Hill defends the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding Arkansans and opposes broad gun-control measures that infringe on those rights. He supports targeted safety measures, including strengthening the National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) and school-safety initiatives, while opposing policies that would broadly limit private gun ownership.

Climate/Energy.stance: French Hill supports an 'all-of-the-above' American energy policy that pursues North American energy independence, protects the environment, and preserves natural resources. He acknowledges climate change is real but opposes the Green New Deal and the Paris Climate Accord as economically harmful. He supports nuclear energy as the cleanest form of base power generation, investing in battery technology and solar innovation, and reducing carbon emissions through American technological innovation rather than international agreements he views as flawed.

Immigration.stance: French Hill supports strong border security and enforcement of immigration laws. He has taken eight trips to the U.S.-Mexico border, backed the Secure the Border Act, the No Sanctuary for Criminals Act, and the Laken Riley Act requiring mandatory detention of illegal immigrants charged with property or violent crimes. He sponsored the Preventing Overdoses and Saving Lives Act 2.0 and the Fentanyl Sanctions Act to combat illicit drugs, and supports securing the border, enforcing existing laws, and legal immigration.

Foreign Policy.stance: French Hill opposes the Ukraine-related legislation as flawed and advocates for a bipartisan, outcome-focused approach to supporting Ukraine that emphasizes accountability and clear strategic objectives. He argues actions should align with U.S. national interests, including border security and domestic economic priorities.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: French Hill has made religious freedom a priority, advocating for the protection of religious minorities worldwide and receiving the 2019 Congressional Champion award from In Defense of Christians for his work on religious liberty. He co-chairs the Congressional HBCU Caucus and supports historically Black colleges and universities in Arkansas. His campaign website states he defends the right to practice religion and protects religious liberty worldwide.

Education.stance: French Hill supports expanding education options beyond traditional four-year degrees, including career and technical education (CTE) programs, apprenticeships, and skilled trades. He advocates allowing Pell Grants and 529 Savings Accounts to fund short-term CTE programs, promoting financial literacy for students, and supporting income sharing agreements as alternatives to student loans. He also co-chairs the Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU) Caucus and has worked to expand educational opportunities at HBCUs in Arkansas.

Election Policy.stance: French Hill supports safeguarding election integrity through voter ID requirements. He voted for the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act (H.R. 8281), which would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. In January 2021, he stated his constitutional duty to certify the Electoral College results while also supporting a commission to review election procedures and irregularities.

candidates.voting_summary: A reliably conservative Republican incumbent serving since 2015, Hill holds a 75% session score and 71% lifetime rating from Heritage Action and a 0% AFL-CIO score in 2025 (12% lifetime). He voted to repeal the Affordable Care Act (2017), supported the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2017), opposed the American Rescue Plan (2021), and voted to establish the January 6 commission — one of 35 Republicans to do so. As Chair of the House Financial Services Committee, he has focused on crypto asset regulation and sponsored 14 enacted bills including the Holding Iranian Leaders Accountable Act and the American Detainee Transparency Act.

voting_sources.title: Rep. French Hill - Scorecard 117 - Heritage Action

candidates.donor_summary: Incumbent French Hill has raised approximately $3.78M in the 2025-2026 cycle as of March 31, 2026, with campaign finance data dominated by the financial services, securities/investment, and banking sectors. Top organizational contributors include Bank of New York Mellon ($46,700), Stephens Inc ($44,645), New York Life Insurance ($44,000), and Coinbase ($41,300), alongside investment firms KKR & Co ($34,000) and Andreessen Horowitz ($17,500). The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) contributed $26,800. The industry breakdown reflects his role as Chair of the House Financial Services Committee and includes significant support from crypto, insurance, and mortgage banking sectors.

candidates.name: Chris Jones
candidates.summary: Chris Jones is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District, having won the March 3 primary. A nuclear engineer with a PhD from MIT and a BS from Morehouse College, he was the Democratic nominee for governor in 2022. Jones campaigns on affordability, healthcare access, and education investment, and in June 2026 received an endorsement from former U.S. Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, who campaigned alongside Jones at a Little Rock rally on Juneteenth.

candidates.voting_summary: Jones has never held legislative office and therefore has no congressional voting record. He was the 2022 Democratic nominee for governor of Arkansas, losing to Sarah Huckabee Sanders; prior to that he served as executive director of the Arkansas Regional Innovation Hub and was appointed by then-Governor Asa Hutchinson to the board of the Arkansas Economic Development Commission's Division of Science and Technology (2020–2022). His campaign platform emphasizes affordability (jobs, rural hospitals, internet access), accountability (fair maps, accessible elections), and opportunity (early childhood education, apprenticeships, technology training), and he has received endorsements from former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and California Governor Gavin Newsom.
candidates.donor_summary: Chris Jones has raised approximately $798,208 in the 2025–2026 cycle as of March 31, 2026, according to FEC filings, with $770,578 coming from individual contributions. Of that total, approximately $220,782 (29%) came from small-dollar unitemized donations, indicating a strong grassroots/small-dollar donor base, while $549,795 came from itemized individual contributions. The campaign also received $18,500 from other committee contributions and $750 from party committees; Jones uses both ActBlue and GoodChange as fundraising platforms and reported $114,411 cash on hand.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of the Arkansas 2nd Congressional District race. French Hill's positions are extensively documented across 12 issue areas with high-confidence citations from official House sources, campaign websites, and credible news outlets. Career history is detailed and internally consistent. Chris Jones's profile appropriately documents his limited public record on most issues with transparent 'no public position found' assessments after good-faith research, while capturing his stated priorities on economy, education, healthcare, and local issues with campaign-sourced citations. The profile maintains neutral language throughout, avoids loaded terminology, and presents both candidates' stances in parallel, non-partisan framing. Minor gaps in Jones's issue coverage reflect the reality of a non-incumbent challenger with a narrower public record, not a quality failure. Donor summaries are detailed and well-sourced from FEC and OpenSecrets. The only minor issues are a handful of unsourced career history entries and one stylistic inconsistency in the Tech & AI section for Jones.

forecast.rationale: French Hill remains the clear favorite based on the district's strong Republican lean, his seven-term incumbency, his chairmanship of House Financial Services Committee, and a massive fundraising advantage (~$3.78M vs. ~$798K). Major nonpartisan forecasters rate this seat Solid/Safe Republican. The only contrary signal is a single May 2026 campaign-commissioned poll (2040 Strategy Group, n=660) showing Democrat Chris Jones leading 46-43, but internal polls typically carry a partisan skew and lack independent verification. Jones is a credible challenger with statewide name recognition from his 2022 gubernatorial run, a strong personal biography (MIT PhD nuclear engineer), and a recent high-profile endorsement from Pete Buttigieg who campaigned with him at a Juneteenth rally in Little Rock. These factors inject some uncertainty but do not overcome the structural Republican advantage in this district. Confidence is medium because public polling is extremely sparse—only one internal poll exists—making it difficult to gauge the true state of the race.
